P86.quantifier_boundary: The internal least-source theorem is exact. Applying it to every nonperiodic Collatz counterexample uses EXT07/P74; nontrivial cycles are separate.
P86.statement: Let S be the least positive source in any shared-future counterexample class whose full shortcut discrepancy is positive at every nonempty prefix and tends to infinity. If an initial safe word d from S reaches Y and a smaller positive V reaches Y through a coefficient-safe word b with c(b)>=c(d), then b followed by the common future has the same two discrepancy properties, contradicting minimality of S.

P87.right_ideal_boundary: A dominated d remains dominated after a common suffix u whenever d|u is coefficient-safe. The unqualified all-suffix statement is not asserted.
P87.statement: For an arbitrary coalescent target a, cut after its unique proper global discrepancy minimum. The nonempty suffix b is strictly coefficient-safe. If a has negative minimum and c(a)>c(d), then c(b)>c(d); positivity, V<S, and literal coalescence remain separate checks.

P88.boundary: No coefficient-safety assumption is needed for injectivity, and no positive ordinary infinite source follows.
P88.decoder: e_j=1 when r_j=2 mod 3, e_j=2 when r_j=1 mod 3, and r_(j-1)=(2^e_j*r_j-1)/3 mod 3^(j-1).
P88.statement: For odd-to-odd gaps e_j in {1,2}, r_j=B_j*2^(-E_j) mod 3^j determines the last exponent from r_j mod 3 and recursively determines the entire finite exponent word; hence the endpoint map is injective at fixed Q.

what_this_result_does_not_prove: Surplus dominance does not show every safe prefix has a dominating ancestor, convert the Q<=17 cutoff into an eventual theorem, prove P80 or H72, exclude cycles, or prove the Collatz conjecture.
